kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Project Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: unbranded / generic (no manufacturer markings printed on the part)
identity.manufacturer_part_number: not specified by ELEGOO, generic part; comparable retail part is Circuit Specialists CEM50-0100
generic_equivalents: Circuit Specialists CEM50-0100 (100uF 50V miniature radial electrolytic capacitor)
identity.package: radial through-hole electrolytic can, larger body than the kit's 10uF capacitor

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A bigger version of the kit's 10uF capacitor. It stores more charge and smooths out bigger, slower dips in power, like the ones a motor or servo causes when it suddenly draws current.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Placed across a motor's or servo's power leads, or right after a battery or power module, to act as a small local reserve of charge so a sudden current draw does not drag down the whole board's voltage.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Same rolled-electrolyte construction as the kit's 10uF capacitor, just with ten times more capacitance, so it can supply a bigger and slightly longer burst of current before it runs low. It is still polarized and must be wired the correct way around.

pinout.name: positive lead (anode)
pinout.notes: the longer of the two leads

pinout.name: negative lead (cathode)
pinout.notes: the shorter lead, on the side marked with a printed stripe down the can

pins.pin_1_identification: The longer lead is positive. The lead next to the printed stripe on the side of the can is negative.

electrical.typical_current: not applicable, passive component with no intrinsic current draw

key_specs.note: ELEGOO's own instruction manual confirms the printed capacitance (100uF) and voltage (50V); detailed tolerance and case dimensions below are from a comparable retail part, not ELEGOO's exact unit.

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A cylindrical aluminum can, noticeably taller and fatter than the kit's 10uF capacitor, closer to the size of a small watch battery in diameter.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Body usually black or dark blue, with white printed text showing the capacitance and voltage directly on the can (for example '100uF 50V'). A pale stripe runs down one side marking the negative lead.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: 100uF, 50V, printed directly rather than as a 3-digit code
easily_confused_with: 10uF electrolytic capacitor: same cylindrical shape and stripe marking, but a visibly smaller body and a different printed value

hazards: installing it backwards (reverse polarity) or exceeding its 50V rating can cause it to heat up, bulge, vent, or in rare cases pop
do not touch a hot or visibly bulging capacitor
handling_notes: always check the negative stripe before powering the circuit
bend leads gently, not sharply right at the body, to avoid cracking the internal seal
common_mistakes: confusing it with the visually similar but smaller 10uF capacitor and using the wrong value

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: capacitor feels warm, the top bulges, or there is a small pop or hiss
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: installed backwards or exposed to more than 50V
symptoms_and_causes.check: power off immediately, verify orientation against the negative stripe, and replace the part if the top is domed or leaking

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: a servo or motor still causes the board to reset or brown out under load
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: capacitor installed backwards, a bad connection, or too small a capacitance for the load
symptoms_and_causes.check: use a multimeter's capacitance mode, expect a reading close to 100uF, and confirm it is wired directly across the motor's or servo's power leads, close to the load

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Discharge the capacitor first by briefly connecting a resistor across its leads, then set the multimeter to capacitance mode; expect a reading close to 100uF.
